items.headline: Wall Street Rebounds Friday, Weekly Losses Persist Amid Bond Market Pressure
items.summary: U.S. equities closed higher on Friday, August 22, trimming losses from a volatile week, but all major indices ultimately ended the week in negative territory. Persistent upward pressure on long-term Treasury yields continued to dominate market sentiment. This digest summarizes the trading activity from the last session on Friday, August 22, 2026, as U.S. markets are closed today, Sunday, August 23, 2026. Not financial advice.

items.headline: Ross Stores Jumps on Upbeat Forecast
items.summary: Ross Stores ($ROST) rallied +4.4% after the company raised its full-year earnings forecast, indicating strong performance.

items.headline: Tesla Rises Despite Recall News
items.summary: Tesla ($TSLA) climbed +5.1% on Friday, closing up $17.73, even as news broke of a major recall of 2.98 million vehicles in China starting September 25 for software updates and warning labels.

items.headline: Bitcoin Surges, Boosting Crypto Stocks
items.summary: Bitcoin ($BTC) surged +9.4% on Friday to trade above $79,000, bringing its weekly gain to +22%. This rally fueled a rise in crypto-related stocks, with Strategy ($MSTR) up +6%, Robinhood ($HOOD) up +13%, and Coinbase ($COIN) up +8%.

items.headline: Klarna Plummets as Week's Top Loser
items.summary: Klarna Group PLC ($KLAR) was the worst-performing stock for the week ending August 22, 2026, experiencing a significant decline of -31.07%.

items.headline: iQIYI Records Steep Weekly Decline
items.summary: iQIYI, Inc. ($IQ) registered the second-largest weekly price decline, falling -22.14% by the end of the trading week.

items.headline: Healthcare and Energy Lead Weekly Sector Performance
items.summary: For the week ending August 22, 2026, Healthcare emerged as the leading sector, gaining +4.19%, followed by Energy, which rose +2.39%. Conversely, Industrials and Utilities were the weakest performers, declining -4.23% and -3.65% respectively. Industrial stocks have shown a strong year-to-date performance, up 16% in 2026, largely due to demand for AI infrastructure, making them the S&P 500's most expensive sector.

items.headline: U.S. Business Activity Remains Solid in August
items.summary: The preliminary S&P Global Composite Purchasing Managers' Index for August increased to 56.04, the highest reading since March 2022, signaling robust business activity. Services PMI also rose to 56.8. This strong activity supports corporate earnings but may reduce urgency for lower interest rates.

items.headline: Treasury Yields Remain Elevated Despite Buyback Efforts; Inflationary Concerns Persist
items.summary: Long-term Treasury yields remained a central concern, with the 10-year yield at 4.73% and the 30-year yield at 5.27% at Friday's close, after briefly receding following the Treasury Department's announcement to double long-bond buybacks to at least $4 billion per operation starting September 9. Inflation continues to be stubbornly high, with the Federal Reserve's preferred measure, the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) report for July, due next week.

items.headline: Nvidia Earnings and Jackson Hole Symposium on Deck Next Week
items.summary: Investors are keenly awaiting Nvidia's ($NVDA) earnings report, scheduled for next Wednesday, which will provide crucial insights into chip demand and AI spending. Additionally, the Jackson Hole symposium (August 27-29) and any comments from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh will be closely watched for signals on monetary policy.

items.headline: Amer Sports Reports Strong Q2 Results and Raised Guidance
items.summary: Amer Sports ($AS) reported a strong second quarter for 2026, with revenue increasing 32% to $1,633 million and adjusted diluted earnings per share reaching $0.22. The company also raised its full-year revenue, margin, and EPS guidance.
